Docket 1.3.87

**Four more findings that were wrong about real sites, now fixed.**

- *Tag and category pages treated as thin articles.* A tag page listing one
  post was told it had "almost no content" and to write more, merge it or
  delete it — advice for an article, not an archive. A busy tag page was also
  reported as "AI-generated copy" because of stock phrases in two excerpts from
  two different posts. Pages whose address marks them as a tag, category or
  author listing are now treated as the archives they are.
- *A collection reported as competing with its own products.* A range's
  collection page shares its name with every product in the range, and that
  joined them all into one "competing pages" group, with advice to redirect
  product pages away. A page listing items for sale no longer competes with
  the products it sells.
- *"No H1 heading" when the H1 holds your logo.* A heading whose only content
  is the logo image is named by that image's alt text, as screen readers and
  search engines read it. A heading that is truly empty is still reported.
- *Shop pages whose products load after the page.* A large page serving only a
  short intro, with its products added by JavaScript, is now reported as what
  was served — with a note to check it in a browser before rewriting anything.

99 checks across 13 areas.
